newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs drop in low volume as prices at ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs drop in low volume as prices at ceiling.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down Friday in insipid trade as investors looked to other markets in the Americas to make their profits, brokers said.
After a sustained rise for Peru's equities in September, investors have decided share prices have reached a temporary ceiling, they added.
Monday was likely to see low volume and narrowly mixed prices, while the market as a whole was not expected to move up for at least a week, they said.
Friday, the General Index fell 0.59 percent to 1,546.17 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index dropped 0.30 percent to 2,095.85 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
In a total of 1,525 trades, 34 fell, 22 stocks rose, and 37 were stable in volume of 18.9 million ($7.4 million).
"There are simply no buy orders for stocks in any tiers. There's no demand," said Percy Romero at local brokerage Fortuna.
However, medium- and long-term prospects for the stock exchange were healthy due to the country's sustained economic growth, brokers said.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru accounted Friday for 18 percent of the market's volume as it remained flat at 5.78 soles.

Among other leaders, Backus y Johnston -- the country's largest brewery -- fell 1.50 percent to 2.63 with eight percent of total volume. Polymetal miner Buenaventura edged up 0.09 percent to 22.00 soles, accounting for 10 percent of the market's volume.
